- **Automated testing**: CI gates with synthetic tenants provide confidence that isolation guarantees hold before deployment.

Tests real-time containment across IAM, perimeter tools, data-layer controls, and recovery. Requires precise policy wording, minimal service disruption, and verifiable rollback.

## Key Concepts
- IAM Deny Policies
- IAM Conditions for conditional bindings
- Access Context Manager perimeters
- VPC Service Controls
- BigQuery Row-Level Security and Column-Level Security
- CMEK rotation and key governance
- Synthetic data testing and rollback auditing

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo: example of a Deny policy fragment (conceptual)
DENY_POLICY {
  deny_condition: { principals: ["serviceAccount:rogue-sa@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com"] }
  permissions: ["bigquery.datasets.get", "storage.objects.get"]
  resource: "projects/PROJECT/datasets/tenant_*"
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the rollback path under high load? 
- Which telemetry would you rely on to detect drift post-containment?

Tests knowledge of storage isolation in a shared bucket using IAM Conditions, signed URLs, and monitoring.

## Key Concepts

- Cloud Storage IAM Conditions
- Signed URLs TTL and tenant binding
- Uniform Bucket Access (no ACLs)
- Cloud Audit Logs and alerting

## Code Example

```javascript
// Example: IAM Condition binding (conceptual)
const binding = {
  role: "roles/storage.objectViewer",
  members: ["user:alice@example.com"],

    title: "TenantIsolation",
    description: "Access only tenant-123 objects",
    expression: "resource.name.startsWith('projects/_/buckets/my-bucket/objects/tenant-123/')"
  }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this isolation in CI and what edge cases would you cover?
- How would you adapt policy if a tenant migrates or is deleted?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design automated, low-downtime containment across complex, multi-brand GCP environments, combining IAM Deny policies, CMEK rotation, PSC/VPC controls, and rollback validation.

## Key Concepts

- IAM Deny policies and Conditions
- CMEK rotation for Secrets Manager and Cloud KMS-backed resources
- VPC Service Controls and Perimeter hardening
- Workload Identity Federation and service account scoping
- Incident response, rollback testing, and pipeline preservation

## Code Example

```yaml
name: projects/PROJECT_ID/denypolicies/containment
deniedPermissions:
  - "secretmanager.secrets.access"
  - "cloudsql.instances.connect"
deniedPrincipals:
  - "principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/POOL_ID/members/*"
deniedResources:
  - "//secretmanager.googleapis.com/projects/PROJECT_ID/secrets/*"
```

## Follow-up Questions

- Compare Deny policies vs IAM Conditions in terms of revocation latency and auditability
- How would you test containment without disrupting live data pipelines?

## Why This Is Asked
Real-world SaaS must meet data residency constraints, not just security per tenant. This question tests architecture for geo-scoped data isolation, cryptographic controls, egress geofencing, and policy enforcement.

## Key Concepts
- Data residency across multi-geo environments
- Per-tenant separation (projects/datasets) and CMEK with rotation
- Private Service Connect and VPC Service Controls for geofenced egress
- Audit trails per tenant in Cloud Logging/Audit Logs
- Policy enforcement with IAM Conditions and an OPA-like runtime check integrated in API layer
- CI/CD validation with synthetic tenants and rollback triggers

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo residency check (illustrative)
function residencyCheck(tenantGeo, resourceGeo) {
  return tenantGeo === resourceGeo;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test CMEK rotation without downtime?
- How to monitor residency violations at scale and alert on anomalies?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical governance, auditability, and detection of cross-tenant access in a real GCP setup.

## Key Concepts
- Cloud Audit Logs with tenant context
- CMEK-protected Cloud Storage + Versioning
- BigQuery exports for analysis
- Cloud Monitoring alerts for anomalies
- CI gate with synthetic tenants and rollback checks

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudocode: verify logs contain tenant_id
async function hasTenantId(logs){ return logs.every(r => 'tenant_id' in r); }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you control log retention and cost?
- How would you ensure logs do not contain PII and comply with regs?
